description: Targeted local-language searching for a CBCG-hosted public-consultation section ('javne konsultacije', 'javna rasprava', 'nacrt odluke', 'rok za dostavljanje komentara') returned no dedicated consultations page under cbcg.me. The site navigation exposes Regulativa, Kljucne funkcije, Publikacije and Javnost rada, but no 'javne rasprave' node was observed in any navigation listing retrieved.

result.result_summary: Consultation on CBCG-originated primary legislation appears to be run by the Ministarstvo finansija on gov.me and the eUprava e-participacija portal instead. Whether CBCG consults publicly on its own secondary Odluke at all remains unresolved and is the single biggest open question for this cell.

why_it_matters: A consultation watch pointed only at cbcg.me would produce systematic false negatives and miss every comment deadline on banking and payments legislation.

description: No RSS/Atom feed, open-data endpoint, or documented API was observed for the saopstenja, podzakonski akti, or register pages during navigation of cbcg.me. All retrieved content was rendered HTML with linked PDFs.

result.result_summary: Change detection for this cell will have to rely on scheduled HTML crawling with content hashing rather than subscribing to a feed. Not verified exhaustively — /rss and sitemap.xml paths were not probed in this pass.

why_it_matters: Drives the collection architecture and cost for the densest source in the run; also means every deadline is discovered on crawl cadence, not push.

description: cbcg.me serves what appears to be the same content under many differing path prefixes observed in indexed results: /me/, /en/, /c/, /r/, /e/, /eng/, and even anomalous prefixes such as /live, /final_kursna.php/ and /luumyaydbzhv.html/. A direct fetch of https://www.cbcg.me/c/o-nama/regulativa/podzakonski-akti returned HTTP 404 while the /me/ equivalent returned content.

result.result_summary: Treated as a routing/canonicalisation quirk, not as a dead source. The 404 on the /c/ variant is a hypothesis about that specific path, not evidence the page is gone.

why_it_matters: Naive crawlers will duplicate content, mis-record 404s as dead sources, and break stored URLs. Canonicalise every cbcg.me URL to the /me/ (or /en/) prefix and dedupe by path suffix and ?id= parameter before storage.

description: The podzakonski akti / Regulations landing pages expose their seven categories as in-page anchor fragments plus direct PDF links rather than as fully addressable per-instrument URLs; individual Odluke are not each given a stable HTML page.

result.result_summary: Per-instrument tracking must key on the PDF href and the 'Sl. list CG br. XX/YY' citation string, not on a per-decision page URL.

why_it_matters: Determines the deduplication and versioning key for the entire regulatory corpus; without it, amendments to an existing Odluka are indistinguishable from new instruments.

description: sluzbenilist.me was located and a document-view URL pattern (/pregled-dokumenta-2/?id={GUID}) was observed, but whether full-text search and document download are free or subscription-gated was not established in this pass, and the site was not fetched directly.

result.result_summary: Access model recorded as unverified. Commercial mirrors (me.propisi.net, katalogpropisa.me) exist precisely because the official gazette is awkward to search, which is weak circumstantial evidence of friction.

why_it_matters: The gazette is the legally authoritative text and the anchor for every effective date; a paywall would force reliance on CBCG-hosted PDFs as the working corpus.

description: English-language queries surfaced the /en/ mirror and Wikipedia but produced no source that local-language queries had not already found, and produced no consultation-related results at all. Local-language querying was strictly higher-yield for this cell.

result.result_summary: Both languages were searched as required; sr queries dominated on recall, en queries were useful only for the mirrored regulation index and for terminology alignment.

why_it_matters: Confirms that the collection design for Montenegro must be sr-first; an en-only pipeline would miss consultations and Council session outputs entirely.

description: Searched for a dedicated national e-consultation portal at ekonsultacije.gov.me, by analogy with Serbia (ekonsultacije.gov.rs) and Republika Srpska (e-konsultacije.vladars.rs).

result.result_summary: No national Montenegrin portal at that address surfaced. The only 'eKonsultacije' hit for Montenegro is the Podgorica municipal platform (ekonsultacije.epodgorica.me). National-level consultations appear instead under the eUprava eParticipacija module (eusluge.euprava.me/eParticipacija/Rasprave/) and on each ministry's own gov.me news feed.

why_it_matters: Prevents the pipeline from being pointed at a non-existent endpoint and confirms that consultation monitoring in Montenegro must be ministry-by-ministry plus eUprava, not a single central register.

description: Attempted an automated fetch of the Official Gazette site http://www.sluzbenilist.me/.

result.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden, no response body. Search results nevertheless show live subpages (/aktuelnosti/) and an active institutional Facebook presence, so this is almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead site. Recorded as UNVERIFIED, not dead.

why_it_matters: The gazette is the legally decisive source for entry-into-force dates. If automated access stays blocked, the collector must either use a browser-profile client or fall back to me.propisi.net mirrors, which introduces a licensing question and a lag risk.

description: Local-language search for a 2026 public consultation on a new/amended Montenegrin AML/CFT law (nacrt zakona o sprječavanju pranja novca i finansiranju terorizma).

result.result_summary: No 2026 javna rasprava for that act was found; hits were dominated by Croatian and Bosnian versions of the similarly-named law, plus existing Montenegrin consolidated texts on gov.me and scmn.me. Evidence of 2024/2025 amendments and a 2026 Constitutional Court decision published in the gazette exists, but no draft in consultation.

why_it_matters: AML/CFT is a core banking-compliance topic; the absence of a current draft is itself intelligence (the file appears to be in an amendment-and-litigation phase rather than a rewrite), but the near-name collision with HR/BA statutes is a real precision hazard for any automated local-language query.

description: Montenegrin legislative vocabulary is shared almost verbatim with Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Republika Srpska ('predlog/prijedlog zakona', 'javna rasprava', 'Službeni list', 'skupština', 'zakoni u proceduri').

result.result_summary: Multiple seed queries returned parlament.gov.rs, propisi.net (Serbia), vladars.rs, parlament.ba and Croatian sources ahead of Montenegrin ones. Reliable disambiguators observed: 'Crne Gore', 'Skupština Crne Gore', 'Vlada Crne Gore', the .me TLD, and the Montenegrin-specific spelling 'predlog' + 'sprječavanje'.

why_it_matters: Without a country qualifier or .me domain filter, an automated local-language crawler for this cell will silently ingest Serbian and Croatian legislation and produce wrong transposition deadlines.

description: Investigated whether tabele usklađenosti (EU transposition correspondence tables), mandatory under Article 40 of the Poslovnik Vlade, are systematically published.

result.result_summary: Individual Izjava/Tabela usklađenosti documents were found filed alongside bills on zakoni.skupstina.me, but Montenegrin civil society has campaigned publicly for these tables to be published as a matter of course, implying coverage is inconsistent. No single searchable register of transposition tables was located.

why_it_matters: These tables are the highest-value artefact in the cell for mapping national provisions to CRD/CRR/PSD/AMLD articles. Inconsistent publication means the collector needs a per-bill harvest strategy and, potentially, freedom-of-information requests.

description: No dedicated, structured register of cross-border 'group decision -> Montenegrin subsidiary effect' was found in any language. Group-level facts must be reconstructed by joining parent-issuer regulated filings (SEOnet, BET, Vienna/Wiener Boerse) with CBCG's own licence register.

result.result_summary: Searches in sr and en returned parent-group IR pages and law-firm guides, but no consolidated regional register linking group decisions to Montenegrin subsidiaries.

why_it_matters: Means the workstream needs a constructed join, not a single feed; increases collection cost and makes the parent-issuer feeds higher priority.

description: The Serbian-language seed query combining parent-bank/subsidiary terms with Montenegro ('matična banka grupa odluka podružnica Crna Gora regulativa') returned only generic NBS statutory pages and no Montenegro-specific regional regulatory items.

result.result_summary: sr-language search surfaced the Zakon o Narodnoj banci Srbije and NBS institutional pages only; nothing on cross-border subsidiary decisions.

why_it_matters: Suggests the local-language vocabulary needs refinement toward deal/consent wording ('saglasnost za sticanje kvalifikovanog učešća', 'prenos vlasništva nad bankom') rather than corporate-structure wording; a naive sr query set will under-retrieve.

description: URLs for ABRS (abrs.ba), Udruženje banaka Srbije (ubs-asb.com), CBBH (cbbh.ba), Addiko IR and EPC were inferred from institutional names and secondary references rather than fetched during this pass.

result.result_summary: Not fetched in this run; recorded with reduced confidence scores.

why_it_matters: These must be confirmed by the deterministic liveness pass before being promoted; a non-200 on first try should be treated as a hypothesis, not a dead source.

description: SeeNews and Paragraf Lex are commercial and at least partly subscription-gated; Bloomberg Adria and eKapija use registration walls on some items.

result.result_summary: Full-text access to the strongest regional cross-border reporting is likely licensed rather than open.

why_it_matters: Budget/licensing decision is required if the workstream depends on early cross-border M&A and supervisory-action reporting; otherwise coverage is headline-only.

description: Montenegrin-language searches using the natural cell vocabulary ('advokatska kancelarija Crna Gora pravni bilten bankarska regulativa', '"Crna Gora" advokati novosti "Zakon o platnom prometu" izmjene analiza obaveze banaka rokovi') did not surface a single Montenegrin law-firm blog or 'pravni bilten' dedicated to banking/payments regulation.

result.result_summary: Local-language results were dominated by firm homepages with no news section, the Bar Association directory, Serbian (RS) firms, and news/regulator pages (CBCG, MINA, Kodex) rather than advisory commentary.

why_it_matters: The A3 assumption that local advisers translate gazette text bilingually holds only weakly in Montenegro: most substantive commentary appears in English via regional firms, so an English-only monitoring design would miss little here — but the local-language layer that does exist likely lives on LinkedIn and in PDFs, not on indexable firm websites.

description: The term 'bankarska garancija' and generic 'advokatska kancelarija' queries pull heavily from Serbian (.co.rs) and Croatian (.hr) sites; 'Zakon o platnom prometu' is also the name of Croatian and Serbian statutes.

result.result_summary: Several top hits for Montenegrin-language queries were Serbian and Croatian legal sites (advokatskakancelarija.slavicajanjic.co.rs, informator.hr), not Montenegrin.

why_it_matters: Any automated local-language collection for this cell must constrain by jurisdiction (site:.me, 'Crna Gora', 'Službeni list Crne Gore', 'CBCG') or it will silently fill with Serbian/Croatian law and produce wrong obligations and deadlines.

description: A substantial share of English-language 'Montenegro law firm' results on crypto/payments licensing are SEO lead-generation pages (e.g. listicles of 'top crypto licensing law firms', unrelated shopping domains recycling licensing copy).

result.result_summary: Searching for Montenegro AML/MiCA/DORA advisory content returned several non-practice sites with legal-sounding but unverifiable claims about licensing timelines and supervisory bodies.

why_it_matters: These pages mimic genuine client alerts and can poison a regulatory-deadline dataset; the pipeline needs a credibility floor and a domain allowlist for this cell.

description: Own websites for Prelevic Law Firm, JPM & Partners Montenegro, Harrisons, and Radonjic/Associates were not resolved within this run; they are recorded via directory profiles only.

result.result_summary: Directory profiles (IFLR1000, Legal 500) confirm the firms exist and rank in banking/finance, but no firm-hosted alert archive URL was observed.

why_it_matters: These are the most likely domestic publishers of Montenegro-specific banking commentary; leaving their domains unresolved is the biggest remaining hole in this cell.

description: No dedicated Montenegro regulatory 'deadline tracker' or implementation-timeline product from any law firm, Big Four member or consultancy was found.

result.result_summary: Deadlines appear only embedded inside individual alerts and country-guide chapters (e.g. instant payments from 20 July 2026, SEPA operational readiness 5 October 2025), never as a maintained tracker.

why_it_matters: Deadline intelligence for ME must be assembled by the collector from scattered alerts plus CBCG primary sources; there is no shortcut product to subscribe to.

description: Searched in Montenegrin for named banks in CBCG penalty coverage (kazna, mjere, kažnjeno pet banaka). Every outlet reports the fines without naming the banks.

result.result_summary: Media consistently relay the CBCG position that supervisory data collected during bank controls is confidential under the AML/CFT law, so the identities of the penalised institutions are not published. Reported scale only: fines of 0.1%-0.5% of regulatory capital, one bank at the 0.5% maximum twice, eleven supervisory measures in the year.

why_it_matters: Media cannot be used to resolve enforcement to the entity level in Montenegro. Entity attribution has to come from other routes (bank annual reports/notes, litigation records, or leaks), so any A3 enforcement tracker must model 'unnamed institution' events.

description: Searched sr for outlets systematically tracking javne rasprave / nacrti zakona deadlines for financial legislation.

result.result_summary: Coverage of consultations is episodic and event-driven (Investitor.me on the Law on Credit Institutions opening; Kodex.me on the Financial Conglomerates consultation closing). No Montenegrin media source maintains a running consultation/deadline register.

why_it_matters: Media alone will miss consultation windows; the media layer must be paired with the government consultation portal (gov.me) and CBCG regulativa pages, with media used for the disputes and reactions rather than the calendar.

description: Searched in English for SeeNews Montenegro banking-supervision coverage.

result.result_summary: No SeeNews Montenegro banking article surfaced in the result set; only BIRN/Balkan Insight results returned. SeeNews may still cover the market behind its subscription wall.

why_it_matters: A likely regional commercial wire remains unconfirmed for this cell; recording it as a candidate would be fabrication, so it is logged as a gap to test directly against seenews.com.

description: Bank-resolution vocabulary was only partially exercised in local language: 'stečaj', 'oduzimanje dozvole' and 'dokapitalizacija' were searched, but 'sanacija', 'privremena uprava', 'privremeni upravnik', 'bail-in' and 'sanacioni organ' were not run as separate queries in this slice.

result.result_summary: Resolution-era coverage (2018-2019 Atlas/IBM temporary administration) was reached indirectly through actor names rather than through the resolution terminology itself.

why_it_matters: Future resolution events will be reported using this untested vocabulary; the keyword set for media monitoring is therefore incomplete and would under-recall a new intervention.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin banking/payments conference brand was found — nothing equivalent to Serbia's or Croatia's recurring banking-sector conferences. Searches in Montenegrin for 'konferencija bankarstvo plaćanja Crna Gora' returned generic economic summits, the capital-market regulator's conference, and Croatian/Serbian events, not a Montenegro-specific payments conference.

result.result_summary: Payments content in Montenegro appears as panels inside broader events (Adria Future Summit, Montenegro Financial Markets) or as CBCG/World Bank workshops, not as a standalone annual conference.

why_it_matters: Collection design must target panel-level metadata inside general events plus regulator workshop announcements, rather than watching for a single sector conference calendar.

description: UBCG (Udruženje banaka Crne Gore) shows no published training/seminar calendar or 'bankarska akademija' equivalent to the Serbian association's Centar za bankarsku obuku, despite explicit Montenegrin-language searching for edukacija/seminari/obuke.

result.result_summary: Only 'O nama' and scattered news items were surfaced; no education section located.

why_it_matters: Association-run training is normally the richest weak signal for forthcoming rules; its apparent absence means the training signal in Montenegro must be picked up from CFA/IIRCG certification providers and CBCG workshops instead.

description: No Montenegrin-language training, certification or job advert was found using PSD2/PSD3 terminology ('PSD2 obuka', 'PSD2 usklađenost', 'zakon o platnom prometu edukacija'). The local vocabulary in evidence is 'platni promet', 'instant plaćanja', 'SEPA' — not the EU directive acronyms.

result.result_summary: PSD2 as a search term is unproductive for Montenegro; SEPA and instant plaćanja are the productive local terms.

why_it_matters: A keyword filter built on EU directive acronyms would miss essentially all Montenegrin payment-regulation weak signals; the glossary must be built on domestic terms.

description: The Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (Montenegrin FIU) was referenced only indirectly; no dedicated vacancy or training page for that body was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Its adverts are presumed to run through uzk.gov.me and zzzcg.me, but this is a hypothesis, not a verified finding.

why_it_matters: FIU staffing is a strong AML-workload indicator; the gap should be closed before the collector is considered complete.

description: Career pages were confirmed only for CKB (TalentLyft ATS) and Prva banka. The remaining licensed banks (NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank AD Podgorica, Lovćen banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Zapad banka, Addiko, Ziraat) were not individually resolved to career URLs in this pass.

result.result_summary: Bank-level hiring coverage is currently partial.

why_it_matters: Instant-payments and compliance hiring at mid-sized banks is exactly the weak signal this cell exists to capture; a partial roster means systematic blind spots.

description: No open-data API, bulk download or data.gov.me-style dataset was located for the CBCG registers of banks, payment institutions or e-money institutions; all appear to be HTML pages (with some PDF/XLS attachments on the enforcement pages).

result.result_summary: Searches in sr and en returned only human-facing register pages; no API documentation surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection must rely on HTML scraping with change-detection, which is brittle against the site reorganisations already visible in cbcg.me URL patterns; budget for snapshotting.

description: No evidence was found of a permanent, searchable archive of CLOSED public consultations with their original attachments — the eUprava e-participacija section surfaces active/recent 'javne rasprave', and a legacy path (eusluge.euprava.me/eParticipacija/Rasprave/) exists but its retention depth was not established.

result.result_summary: Local-language search 'javna rasprava arhiva nacrt zakona' returned individual consultation pages and ministry news items, not a closed-consultation archive index.

why_it_matters: Consultation drafts and deadline notices are exactly the content that disappears; without an official archive, Wayback/Save-Page-Now capture on first sighting becomes mandatory rather than optional.

description: No public CBCG register of currency-exchange offices (mjenjačnice) or of payment-service agents operating on a cross-border/passporting basis was located in this pass, and no register of 'mjenice' (promissory notes) was confirmed despite the local term being searched.

result.result_summary: Search on 'mjenica'/'blokirani računi' returned only the forced-collection (prinudna naplata) pages, not a separate bill-of-exchange register.

why_it_matters: If such registers exist off the main navigation, a whole class of regulated actors is missing from the seed list; if they do not exist, that absence itself is a structural finding about ME supervision transparency.

description: Local-language queries for 'Agencija za nadzor osiguranja' and 'Komisija za vrijednosne papire' return predominantly Bosnian/Federation-of-BiH institutions (ano.ba, azobih.gov.ba, komvp.gov.ba) rather than Montenegrin ones.

result.result_summary: Montenegrin entities resolved only as ano.me and scmn.me after manual disambiguation.

why_it_matters: Noisy terms: any automated query expansion in sr must be domain-pinned to .me (and to Podgorica) or the corpus will be contaminated with BiH and RS regulators.

description: The company register is reachable through at least four distinct hosts (crps.me, pretraga.crps.me, efirma.tax.gov.me, irms.tax.gov.me), several still on plain HTTP, suggesting an in-progress migration to the Tax Administration IRMS platform.

result.result_summary: All four hosts appeared in search results for the same registry function.

why_it_matters: Any hard-coded CRPS URL is likely to break; the collector should resolve the register through a small host-priority list and record which host answered.

description: All URLs in this slice are recorded from search-engine results and inferred site structure; none were fetched and none should be treated as liveness-verified. Some cbcg.me URLs seen in indexes contain corrupted path fragments (e.g. /cuymrbfb.html/, /sliNe_i_fajlovi/), which are hypotheses about legacy or mangled paths rather than confirmed routes.

result.result_summary: Liveness deliberately left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: The verifier should canonicalise cbcg.me paths and, on 404, retry the equivalent /me/ and /en/ prefixes before marking anything dead.

description: Montenegro is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so BIS Red Book payment and FMI statistics do not contain a Montenegro series. Searches surfaced only the CPMI methodology (d168), the BIS data portal and the CBCG's own RTGS/DNS statistics.

result.result_summary: No Montenegro rows found in the BIS CPMI Red Book dataset; BIS value for this cell is methodological/comparative only.

why_it_matters: Payment-system benchmarking for Montenegro must be built from CBCG-published RTGS/DNS data normalised to the CPMI schema, not pulled from BIS directly.

description: No evidence was found of an EBA or ECB opinion, guideline or assessment addressed specifically to Montenegro beyond the SEE Memorandum of Cooperation (2015), the ECB-CBCG MoU (2018) and the professional-secrecy equivalence assessment.

result.result_summary: EBA/ECB engagement with Montenegro appears to be framework-level (MoU, equivalence) rather than country-opinion-level.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale's expectation of 'EBA/ECB opinions' on Montenegro is only partially met; monitoring effort should be weighted toward MONEYVAL, IMF and the EC enlargement report instead.

description: No established Montenegrin-language terminology was found for BIS/CPMI concepts (Red Book, financial market infrastructures) or for credit-rating methodology terms; domestic coverage uses English terms or loose paraphrase.

result.result_summary: Local-language search for BIS/CPMI and rating-agency methodology in Montenegrin returned no usable native glossary.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring for those sub-topics must rely on the English acronyms (BIS, CPMI, Moody's, S&P, Fitch, Ba3) embedded in Montenegrin-language text rather than on translated terms.

description: Full rating reports from Moody's, and the expert edition of the Basel AML Index, are behind subscription or licensing.

result.result_summary: Only press releases, outlook summaries and the free public ranking are openly accessible.

why_it_matters: A rating-driven early-warning feed for Montenegro cannot be built from primary CRA text alone; it must lean on free regulatory-disclosure pages (S&P) plus secondary trade-press relay (SeeNews, MINA, bankar.me).

description: Several canonical landing-page URLs in this slice (MONEYVAL Montenegro jurisdiction page, IMF country page, EBRD Montenegro country page, Moody's Montenegro issuer page, Montenegro FIU subsite) were constructed from the publishers' standard URL patterns and from search-result context rather than opened directly.

result.result_summary: Deep-link example_urls came from search results and are high confidence; the top-level landing URLs are pattern-inferred and should be treated as unverified pending the deterministic liveness pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents a false 'verified' claim; the liveness pass should prioritise these landing pages, and a 403/timeout on coe.int or imf.org should be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

description: The standalone 'Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma' with a presumed domain upn.gov.me could not be found as a live independent site. All current evidence points to the function having been absorbed into the Police Administration as the 'Sektor za finansijsko-obavještajne poslove' at gov.me/foj.

result.result_summary: No upn.gov.me page surfaced in either local-language or English searching; gov.me/foj resolved and returned a full navigation.

why_it_matters: A collection plan keyed to the old directorate name or a guessed upn.gov.me domain would silently collect nothing. The FIU must be tracked under gov.me/foj and under 'finansijsko-obavještajni' terminology, not only under 'Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca'.

description: The FIU site (gov.me/foj) exposes news, legal framework, obliged-entity and sanctions pages, but no discrete 'Smjernice' (guidance) or 'Izvještaji' (reports) section was visible in navigation. The obliged-entities page links out to CBCG for beneficial-owner instructions.

result.result_summary: Navigation enumerated; guidance appears dispersed across the obliged-entities page, gov.me/dokumenta and CBCG rather than centralised.

why_it_matters: AML guidance for Montenegro cannot be collected from one FIU URL; a multi-target harvest (FIU obveznici page + gov.me/dokumenta + CBCG + ANO + KTK) is required, otherwise guidance will appear absent.

description: https://www.azlp.me/me/ returned HTTP 404 on fetch, while https://www.azlp.me/me/preporuke fetched successfully and revealed the full navigation.

result.result_summary: 404 on the assumed locale root; sibling paths live. Treated as a routing quirk, not a dead site.

why_it_matters: A crawler seeded on the /me/ root would report the DPA as unreachable. Seeds must point at real section paths (/me/preporuke, /me/zastita-licnih-podataka) or the bare domain.

description: Three distinct consultation surfaces appeared: euprava.gov.me/e-participacija (state), ekonsultacije.epodgorica.me (Podgorica municipality), and per-ministry javne rasprave pages. The generic 'ekonsultacije.gov.me' host named in the seed framing was not directly confirmed.

result.result_summary: State consultations confirmed on euprava.gov.me/e-participacija and on ministry pages; the municipal eKonsultacije platform is a different, local-government scope.

why_it_matters: Seeding the municipal portal would produce irrelevant Podgorica planning consultations and miss national financial-sector drafts.

description: No Montenegrin-language term or dedicated institution was found for a financial-services ombudsman or an out-of-court ADR body for banking disputes outside the CBCG. Consumer redress paths located were: ANO's prigovori channel (insurance), the Market Inspection (general consumer protection), and CEZAP (NGO).

result.result_summary: Searches in Montenegrin on consumer protection in financial services returned only the general Consumer Protection Law framework, the inspectorate and the NGO.

why_it_matters: If such a body exists under a name I did not guess, complaint-level intelligence on banks and payment firms is being missed. Needs a targeted follow-up on the Consumer Protection Law text for named redress bodies.

description: Montenegro's CRS/AEOI status is contradictory across sources: one source suggests AEOI-standard exchange as of January 2026, another states Montenegro failed to meet CRS MCAA requirements and lacks the necessary IT system. FATCA in force since 2018 is the only firm fact.

result.result_summary: No authoritative Montenegrin tax-authority page confirming CRS reporting obligations or deadlines for financial institutions was located.

why_it_matters: CRS go-live would create hard, dated reporting obligations for every Montenegrin bank. The status must be resolved against the tax authority and the OECD AEOI portal before it can be used.

description: Local-language AML queries are heavily contaminated by Croatian and Serbian results (mfin.gov.hr, hgk.hr, paragraf.rs, KPMG Serbia) because the terminology is near-identical across the region ('sprječavanje/sprečavanje pranja novca', 'obveznici', 'smjernice').

result.result_summary: Roughly half of first-page results on the seed AML query were non-Montenegrin.

why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on these terms without a .me / 'Crna Gora' constraint will ingest the wrong jurisdiction's rules — a serious correctness risk for a compliance-deadline product.

description: Several bodies serve content from two path/domain generations simultaneously: azlp.me uses both /docs/ and /storage/docs/; ano.me uses both clean URLs and legacy Joomla index.php query strings; cezap.me coexists with cezap.org.

result.result_summary: Live documents observed on both variants for AZLP and ANO.

why_it_matters: Deduplication and link-rot handling must treat these as the same source; a naive crawler will either double-count or drop the legacy archive, which holds the older decisions and guidance.

description: No standalone, publicly navigable page for the Chapter 9 working group (radna grupa za poglavlje 9 - finansijske usluge) — membership, meeting minutes, or its own progress reports — was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: sr queries on 'radna grupa poglavlje 9' returned only generic Ministry of European Affairs proposal PDFs referencing other chapters (2, 12, 27); no Ch.9 working-group artefact surfaced.

why_it_matters: Working-group documents would give the earliest view of planned financial-services transposition; without them the earliest signal is the annual accession programme.

description: The TAIEX events database could not be resolved to a concrete, country-filterable search URL for Montenegro financial services.

result.result_summary: Search returned TAIEX policy/landing pages and annual activity report PDFs, but no working query endpoint or Montenegro financial-services event list.

why_it_matters: TAIEX events are among the most granular leading indicators of which specific EU acts an administration is preparing to transpose; leaving it unindexed loses lead time.

description: No Montenegrin-language terminology was identified for the EU-side technical assistance instruments (TAIEX, twinning) as used in official ME communications during this pass; the twinning material found was in English or Croatian.

result.result_summary: sr searching for these instruments in a Montenegrin context returned Serbian (mei.gov.rs) and Croatian (hnb.hr) sources rather than ME-domestic pages.

why_it_matters: Local-language search coverage for the technical-assistance sub-cell is weaker than for the legislative sub-cell; ME-side twinning announcements may be being missed.

description: Serbian EU-integration portals (mei.gov.rs) rank highly for Montenegrin chapter-9 queries because the terminology is near-identical across sr variants.

result.result_summary: The top sr result for the seed chapter-9 query was Serbia's Ministry of European Integration guide, not a Montenegrin source.

why_it_matters: A naive collector keyed on 'poglavlje 9 finansijske usluge' will ingest Serbian material as Montenegrin; country scoping must be enforced at the domain level (.me, eu.me, gov.me).

description: Both EC document downloads and Montenegrin gov.me documents are served from opaque GUID-based URLs with no stable slug.

result.result_summary: Observed enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/<guid> and wapi.gov.me/download/<guid> patterns across all document hits.

why_it_matters: Link rot is near-certain between editions; the collector must archive bytes on first fetch and re-resolve links from parent pages rather than storing document URLs as identifiers.

description: No national payment-QR standard for Montenegro was found. Searching 'QR kod plaćanje standard' in Serbian/Montenegrin returned Serbia's NBS IPS QR ecosystem and Montenegro's fiscal-invoice QR requirement, but no CBCG-issued payment QR specification, generator or validator.

result.result_summary: Local-language QR queries surfaced only fiscalisation QR (tax invoices) for Montenegro; the payment-initiation QR hits were all Serbian (ips.nbs.rs) or unrelated (QRIS, QR Ph).

why_it_matters: A national QR overlay is a normal follow-on to an instant-payment go-live and would carry merchant/PSP technical deadlines. Its apparent absence is itself intelligence: either it does not yet exist, or it lives inside not-yet-public instant-payment scheme documentation.

description: No domestic card switch / national card scheme operator was identified for Montenegro — no equivalent of a DinaCard, BKM or national ATM-sharing network with its own rulebook and participant circulars.

result.result_summary: Searches for a Montenegrin card switch returned only international schemes (Visa/Mastercard), bank lists, and third-party processors (ChipCard/ASEE, Ingenico POS at NLB Montenegro). No designated domestic scheme body surfaced.

why_it_matters: If no national card scheme exists, card-side rule changes for Montenegro originate from Visa/Mastercard global releases plus CBCG regulation, which changes where the collection effort should point. This needs confirmation, not assumption.

description: I had no confirmed Montenegrin-language brand or acronym for a domestic card scheme or switch to search with, so the card-scheme leg of this cell was searched mainly with English and generic Serbian terms.

result.result_summary: Queries used generic terms ('kartično procesiranje', 'card scheme', vendor names). Without a real local brand name, recall is likely incomplete.

why_it_matters: Local-language coverage for the card-scheme sub-topic is weaker than for instant payments and RTGS/DNS; a missed local brand would mean a missed rulebook publisher.

description: The CBCG instant payments (TIPS Clone) page could not be retrieved on the single attempt made.

result.result_summary: WebFetch to https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone returned 'socket hang up'. The page is indexed and internally linked, so this is a transport/anti-bot hypothesis, not evidence the page is dead.

why_it_matters: This is the single most important page in the cell. The collector must use browser-like headers, retries and locale fallbacks rather than marking it unreachable.

description: No standalone web presence was found for the Nacionalni odbor za platni promet (National Payment Board) — no agenda, minutes or membership page.

result.result_summary: Only broadcaster reporting and CBCG press mentions describe its formation (pending parliamentary action) and its SEPA-review meetings.

why_it_matters: Its meeting outcomes are likely to set participant readiness milestones; without a primary publication channel, this governance layer can only be tracked indirectly and with lag.

description: No consolidated 'Nacionalna strategija platnog prometa' (national payment strategy) document for Montenegro was located.

result.result_summary: Local-language strategy queries returned the fiscal strategy 2024-2027 and EU-affairs documents instead; payments direction appears to be set through the Law on Payment Transactions, CBCG odluke and the National Payment Board rather than a named standalone strategy.

why_it_matters: Absence of a single strategy document means forward-looking migration windows must be assembled from law drafts, CBCG decisions and board outcomes — a materially different collection design.

description: The CBCG e-money register page states that no electronic money institution is currently entered in the register.

result.result_summary: Fetched https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/registri/registar-institucija-za-elektronski-novac-i-njihovih-agenata; page text: 'U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac'.

why_it_matters: The ME operator-side payments cell currently has no domestic EMI at all — all e-money-like propositions must be foreign, bank-issued, or structured as payment services. Any future entry is a first-of-kind market event and should be a high-priority alert.

description: No corporate websites were located for the licensed PIs MONETA MNE DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO or 'Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o' despite local-language searching.

result.result_summary: Search for these names returned only unrelated airport-transfer and tourism content; 'Montenegro Transfers' is a highly noisy term colliding with the travel sector.

why_it_matters: Several licensed operators may have no public web presence, meaning the CBCG register PDFs and CRPS filings are the only reliable trace of them — collection design must not assume an operator website exists.

description: An Alta Pay Montenegro website (e.g. altapay.me) was not confirmed in this pass, only the Serbian group site, social pages and a business-directory profile carrying office@altapay.me.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced altapay.rs group news, LinkedIn/Facebook pages and companywall.me profile; no ME corporate domain confirmed.

why_it_matters: Operator news for this licensee may only exist on group-level Serbian channels, which changes the monitoring locus for one of the larger ME PI groups.

description: No Montenegrin-language terminology was found for a domestic instant-payment consumer wallet brand or an open-banking/API access scheme; coverage of instant payments is expressed only via bank channels ('instant plaćanja', TIPS Clone) with no separate app.

result.result_summary: Local reporting states the service runs through existing bank e-channels with no new account or app required.

why_it_matters: There is currently no wallet-operator layer to scout in ME; the operator-side payments story is bill-payment/remittance PIs plus banks, not wallet fintechs.

description: No evidence found that Payten or AllSecure operate a Montenegro-specific presence; only regional/Croatian PSP material surfaced.

result.result_summary: Search returned Monri/WSPay Croatian material and generic Montenegro card-acceptance tourism pages.

why_it_matters: The acquiring/gateway vendor layer serving ME merchants remains unmapped and needs a dedicated follow-up pass with merchant-side (checkout page) evidence.

description: No Montenegrin bank was found publishing a document explicitly branded 'Stub 3' / 'Pillar 3'. The equivalent artefact is published under the local term 'javno objelodanjivanje/objavljivanje podataka i informacija' with a reference date, citing the Law on Credit Institutions and CBCG disclosure regulation.

result.result_summary: The seed query 'godišnji izvještaj banke Crna Gora objelodanjivanje Stub 3' returned only EBA/BIS/Canadian/Maltese Pillar 3 material and no ME bank document; the local-term query returned the real artefacts (Addiko, CKB, Prva banka).

why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on 'Pillar 3'/'Stub 3' will miss the entire Montenegrin disclosure corpus. Query templates must use 'objelodanjivanje podataka' / 'objavljivanje podataka i informacija' instead.

description: https://www.ckb.me/ could not be fetched: TLS error 'unable to verify the first certificate'.

result.result_summary: Root fetch failed on certificate chain, while document URLs on the same host (opsti-uslovi PDFs, tarifnik, 2024 auditor report) appeared in search results, so the site is almost certainly live with an incomplete intermediate chain.

why_it_matters: The market-leading bank must not be recorded as dead. The collector for ckb.me needs a fetcher tolerant of chain issues (or a full CA bundle), and CBCG's mirror is the fallback for its financial statements.

description: Homepage fetches of nlb.me, erstebank.me, lovcenbanka.me and prvabankacg.com surfaced only product marketing; none exposed a discoverable, dated 'obavještenja za klijente' archive to the fetcher.

result.result_summary: Four of the largest banks' homepages returned no notice-index URL; notice content appears to live in JS-rendered news carousels or one-off PDF links rather than a stable archive.

why_it_matters: Customer notices are the earliest evidence signal in this cell, and for most banks they are not archived at a stable URL — a snapshot-and-diff collector (or headless rendering) is required rather than a simple RSS/index crawl, and historical notices may be unrecoverable.

description: Local-language queries strongly pull in same-brand entities from BiH and Serbia (asabanka.ba, nlb-rs.ba, nlbkb.rs, addiko.rs, adriaticbank.rs) whose notices use nearly identical wording.

result.result_summary: Several top hits for 'obavijest/obavještenje o izmjeni opštih uslova' were Bosnian or Serbian banks, not Montenegrin ones.

why_it_matters: Any collector must hard-filter on Montenegrin domains/entity names, otherwise the cell will be polluted with out-of-jurisdiction notices that look authentic. 'Obavijest' (BiH/HR spelling) vs 'obavještenje' (ME/RS) is a useful discriminator but not sufficient.

description: The routine playbook at C:/Users/User/Dropbox/... is a Windows path and does not exist on this macOS host; method was applied from the task brief only.

result.result_summary: No playbook file read.

why_it_matters: Classification vocabulary and scoring calibration may drift from the canonical routine definition.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin fintech, payment-institution, e-money or leasing industry association was found despite targeted local-language searching.

result.result_summary: Searches combining 'udruženje', 'fintech', 'platne institucije' and Montenegro returned only the banking association, the chamber's mixed banking/insurance board and insurance bodies. Non-bank payment providers appear to be represented, if at all, through UBCG's digitalisation/fintech committee or the chamber, not through a body of their own.

why_it_matters: For sector=payments this is a structural coverage hole: there is no association-level aggregator of PSP positions, so PSP views on regulation must be collected firm-by-firm or via UBCG committee output.

description: UBCG does not appear to publish its consultation responses / position papers in a dedicated, systematic section of its own website.

result.result_summary: Fetching ubcg.info/blog/ showed institutional announcements (assembly, awards, workshops, Bankar issues) from Dec 2025 to Jun 2026 with no draft-law or formal consultation items; concrete UBCG positions (Draft Law on Bank Resolution comments; AML/CFT amendment support; banking-secrecy proposal) surfaced only through press reporting. No RSS feed was visible on the blog page.

why_it_matters: The most valuable A3 content from this cell exists but is not primary-published, so collection must be triangulated via gov.me public-discussion reports and specialist press rather than via a single association feed.

description: Three komora.me URLs returned by search (the banking/finance/insurance association board page, the associations index, and the legislation page) each returned HTTP 404 when fetched.

result.result_summary: https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenje-bankarstva-i-drugih-finansijskih-organizacija-i-osiguranja, https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenja-2 and https://komora.me/en/cem/zakonodavstvo all 404'd, while the komora.me homepage fetched normally. The pages are indexed with content, so this reads as CMS slug churn, not removal.

why_it_matters: The chamber's banking board is a core cell source; recorded as unverified/hypothesis rather than dead. Slugs must be re-resolved from the live sitemap before any scheduled collection is configured.

description: No public, machine-readable member directory was located for Privredna komora Crne Gore, AmCham Montenegro, MFIC or Unija poslodavaca within this pass.

result.result_summary: Only leadership/board-composition fragments were retrieved (PKCG board president and secretary names; MFIC and MEF descriptive membership claims). Full member lists were not confirmed on any of the four sites.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale leans on member directories as the cheapest pointer to the full actor population; only UBCG (11 banks) and the insurance bureau delivered that reliably.

description: Two competing accountancy/audit institutes exist (ISRCG at isrcg.org and IRRCG at irrcg.co.me), plus a separate internal-audit institute (IIRCG at iircg.co.me), with overlapping names and certifications.

result.result_summary: IIRCG advertises an 'Ovlašćeni računovođa' certificate despite being the internal-auditors institute, and ISRCG also covers internal auditors — the naming and remit overlap is genuine, not a search artefact.

why_it_matters: Entity resolution risk: a collector keyed on 'institut ... revizora Crne Gore' will conflate three distinct bodies and mis-attribute positions on audit/accounting rules.

description: Neither English nor Montenegrin queries surfaced a concrete, currently open tender for a banking-supervision information system in Montenegro (e.g. a CBCG supervisory reporting / SupTech / credit registry procurement) in general web search results.

result.result_summary: General portal and aggregator pages were returned; the only concrete CBCG procurement artefact found via search was a publication-printing service award. This is consistent with such notices living inside CeJN's search interface, which general web search indexes poorly.

why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be served by web search alone — the collector must query the CeJN portal (and TED/ECEPP) programmatically rather than relying on search-engine discovery.

description: No CeJN machine-readable feed, open-data export or documented API was identified during this pass; only the HTML tender listing at cejn.gov.me/tenders was observed in results.

result.result_summary: Search returned the portal landing/tenders pages and a demo instance (portal-jn-demo-web.azurewebsites.net) but no API/OpenData documentation.

why_it_matters: Collection design for the most important source in this cell may require HTML scraping and session handling rather than a clean feed; a demo instance existing suggests the underlying platform may expose predictable endpoints worth probing in the verification pass.

description: The CBCG tender page URL was returned in a Montenegrin-language variant path (/e/javnost-rada/tenderi-i-oglasi). The parallel /me/ path was not directly observed, and no fetch was performed.

result.result_summary: URL taken from search results only; liveness and language-path stability are unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should test both /me/ and /e/ paths before recording the source as reachable or dead.

description: The procurement review body appears under two names: the older 'Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki' and what appears to be a successor/renamed 'Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki' at kontrola-nabavki.me. The exact current legal name and whether an older domain still serves archives was not resolved.

result.result_summary: Both names appear in live results; kontrola-nabavki.me/rjesenja is the observed live decisions listing.

why_it_matters: Historical decision archives may sit on a retired domain; failing to resolve this risks losing several years of dispute history that documents delayed financial-sector IT projects.

description: No Montenegrin-language interface or notice channel was found for TED, ECEPP, UNGM, World Bank or EIB notices concerning Montenegro; all IFI/EU notices in this cell appear to be English-only.

result.result_summary: Local-language queries for IFI notices returned only Montenegrin-language secondary coverage (EU Delegation, eu.me), not the notice systems themselves.

why_it_matters: Local-language keyword monitoring will systematically miss donor-funded tenders; the collector needs a separate English keyword set plus country-code filters for the IFI layer.

description: Several tender aggregators covering Montenegro (globaltenders, tendersinfo, tendersontime, tender-service, tenderspedia, tendersgo) appear in results but are subscription-gated SEO properties of low evidentiary value.

result.result_summary: Their pages restate that notices exist without reproducing primary content.

why_it_matters: They should be explicitly excluded from the source register to avoid diluting it with low-credibility, non-collectable intermediaries.

description: No AML/regtech vendor (NICE Actimize, Oracle FCCM, SAS, ComplyAdvantage, Sanction Scanner, Tonbeller/FICO, etc.) was found publishing a named Montenegrin bank customer reference or case study.

result.result_summary: English and local-language searches returned only generic global 'top AML software' listicles and Croatian/Serbian SPNFT tools (SPNFT.hr, Potecon, SPINIFT) with no Montenegro bank reference.

why_it_matters: AML/regtech is a live spend area under EU-accession pressure, but the supply side is invisible in public sources. The vendor-reference route fails here and must be replaced by an alternative (bank annual reports, CBCG supervisory guidance, job ads naming AML tools).

description: No Montenegro-specific ATM hardware contract or customer reference found on Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos channels.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced only global manufacturer strategy coverage and the Bankart/Diebold SEE middleware announcement; no Montenegro bank named.

why_it_matters: ATM fleet ownership in Montenegro appears to be intermediated by Payten rather than contracted directly with OEMs, which changes where the buying signal lives; the OEM channel is a weak collection point for this market.

description: Local-language vendor vocabulary for the supplier side is thin: Montenegrin/Serbian sources overwhelmingly use English-in-local terms ('core banking', 'POS', 'SoftPOS', 'processing') rather than native equivalents.

result.result_summary: Queries built on 'dobavljač', 'rješenje', 'implementacija', 'kartično poslovanje' returned mostly bank retail pages and generic portals; productive local queries were the ones mixing English product nouns with sr grammar.

why_it_matters: Future collection must use mixed-language query templates ('banka + core banking + Crna Gora') rather than pure-sr translations, or recall will collapse.

description: No public core-banking platform attribution found for Hipotekarna banka, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Universal Capital Bank or Lovćen banka.

result.result_summary: Only regulator register entries and bank profiles returned; no vendor named a core system at any of these institutions.

why_it_matters: The core-banking layer is the least visible part of the private-bank stack in Montenegro; digital-channel and ATM/POS layers are far better documented. Attribution here will need indirect fingerprinting (job ads, app metadata, SWIFT/ISO integration tenders, staff LinkedIn skill tags).
